newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds, futures choppy, downside risk ahead.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds, futures choppy, downside risk ahead.

text.p: German debt prices wobbled in late Friday trade and remained in positive territory with the help of firmer U.S. Treasuries.
But traders said the market looked toppish and was at risk of coming off in the early part of next week.
"We may not have quite topped out yet, but there is a slight negative bias now," said one London-based trader.

He said a double top plotted by the LIFFE June Bund future at 101.80 and 101.82 was a negative signal on daily charts. The DTB June Bund hit a high at 101.79 on Friday, but was untraded on Thursday with German markets closed for May Day.
The DTB June Bund future was trading 28 basis points higher on the day at 101.55 by 1413 GMT, while the 10-year cash benchmark Bund was at 101.81 for a 5.741 percent yield.

"For today, we could go a bit higher from current levels in late trade, maybe back to around 101.65, but then we will start to head lower, targeting the 101.20 region," said a technical analyst based in Stuttgart.
Traders said the market was choppy in afternoon business, with slim volumes making price movements more exaggerated.
"We spent most of the session trading at the higher end of the range, but the volumes were thin and activity pretty slow."
On spreads, the 10-year Bund/T-note gap stood at 106 basis points by 1424 GMT as the German and U.S. markets remained in step.
